ideas.name: Palantir Technologies Inc.
ideas.thesis: Palantir just delivered one of the most decisive earnings beats in its history: Q2 revenue of $1.94B crushed the $1.81B consensus (+93% YoY), adj EPS of $0.41 beat the $0.35 estimate, and US commercial revenue surged 149% YoY to $764M. Management raised FY26 revenue guidance to $8.15-8.158B -- dramatically above the prior upper limit of ~$7.66B and well above the prior Street consensus of ~$7.7B. The stock was up ~27-30% after hours from its $125.65 regular-session close, and a wave of analyst PT upgrades followed this morning.

Options are highly active today (flagged as 'notable open interest changes' and 'early notable gainers among liquid option names') -- defined-risk call spreads or long calls may offer better risk/reward than outright stock given the already large overnight gap.
ideas.bull_case: US commercial revenue compounding at 380% since 2024 and now tracking to $3.42B+ for FY26 suggests the AI platform transition is not slowing. If PLTR re-rates toward the $200+ targets now held by multiple banks, the stock has 30-40%+ upside from the AH print.

Forward P/S remains extremely elevated (north of 60x even post-guidance raise), and any macro risk-off or profit-taking wave could erase a significant portion of the gap quickly. Historical 'buy the print' setups at these valuations have often faded within days.

ideas.name: The Boeing Company
ideas.thesis: The FAA's certification of the 737 MAX 7 on Aug 3 -- after nearly a decade of delays -- is a meaningful milestone in Boeing's financial recovery narrative, with ~30 completed aircraft ready for final retrofit and Southwest deliveries starting early 2027. Boeing's Q2 results (reported July 28) already showed 171 aircraft deliveries (highest since 2018), positive FCF of $631M (first time since 2018), and a record backlog of $715B. Today's MAX 7 certification triggered a fresh wave of analyst upgrades: BNP Paribas upgraded to Outperform, JPMorgan raised target to $290, Goldman raised to $260, RBC to $265.
ideas.catalyst: FAA 737 MAX 7 certification issued Aug 3, 2026 -- clearing path for deliveries and production ramp. Next major undated catalyst: 777X FAA certification (still in queue, expected 2026-2027 per management).
ideas.edge: Median analyst 12-month target ~$273 (28 analysts) vs today's price ~$236-237, implying ~15-17% upside. JPMorgan's revised target of $290 implies ~23% upside. Options available for defined-risk exposure. Boeing generated its first positive FCF since 2018 in Q2 ($631M), validating the recovery thesis with a hard number.
ideas.bull_case: MAX 7 certification de-risks the production ramp story; if 777X follows in 2026, the multiple could re-rate sharply higher as FCF visibility improves toward management's $1-3B FY26 target.
ideas.bear_case: MAX 7 is a slow-selling variant (less than 6% of backlog) and won't enter passenger service until early 2027 -- the market may have already priced this milestone. Free cash flow remains volatile, EASA certification for MAX 7 has not been pursued, and the company still trails Airbus significantly in order and delivery volumes.
